knowledge_cards.note: Read for the PostgreSQL vs ClickHouse split and the client timeout story. Wiki was not edited. A post-approval note can record where CH HTTP failures gain SQL context.

precedents.relevance: Every ClickHouse HTTP call ends in private request(). Failures throw ClickhouseException with the parsed message only. Line 438. SQL, route, query_id, and elapsed stay off the exception.
precedents.applicable: The enricher has to run where the SQL is still in scope: public select() and write() on a platform subclass. Do not edit the package in this ticket.

precedents.relevance: Illuminate QueryException logs context.sql to the db-error channel. ClickhouseException is a RuntimeException, so it falls through to the generic catch, which logs message, code, file, and line, and not SQL.
precedents.applicable: Match the existing context.sql key so scripts/extract_sql_queries.py can see CH failures. Leave the trait's retry and empty-state behavior alone.

precedents.relevance: Catch ClickhouseException, log a thin db-error line (org_id, message, code), emit clarity.query_timeout, and return an empty collection outside debug.
precedents.applicable: A client wrapper still sees these failures before the catch. Rethrow the original exception so this swallow stays intact.

precedents.relevance: Logs exception class, message, code, file, and line to db-error. No SQL. Uses clarity.query_error, not clarity.query_timeout.
precedents.applicable: Do not relabel that metric. The new line is an additional structured log, not a replacement of this counter.

precedents.relevance: In production and testing, Throwable is report()'d and the method returns []. report() hits the default log, not db-error. bootstrap/app.php only counts Illuminate QueryException SQLSTATE 57014.
precedents.applicable: An exception-handler hook misses every swallowed ClickhouseException. The enricher belongs on the HTTP client, which runs before those catches.

precedents.relevance: JsonFormatter plus a processor that adds user id, name, and email, and on error-and-above the org id and name.
precedents.applicable: User and org are already on the channel. New context should add user_id and org_id and should not add another copy of the email. Do not change the processor in this ticket.

precedents.relevance: Reads context.sql from each JSON log line and skips lines that lack it.
precedents.applicable: Put the truncated statement in context.sql.

precedents.status: shipped write-path connect budget, cited in config/database.php and okf/concepts/clickhouse-integration.md
precedents.relevance: Read path stays timeout_connect 2s and timeout_query 60s. Write path uses a longer connect budget and one retry. Server max_execution_time is 0, so the 60s cap is client-side.
precedents.applicable: Copy those numbers into the log context. Do not change them.

precedents.relevance: QUERY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS is 60. OBSERVED_MAX_LATENCY_SECONDS is 33.7. Lock TTLs are sized off that client timeout and the proxy budget.
precedents.applicable: Soft collision. Do not retune those constants or the cache locks.

precedents.relevance: First Glance 43033 lists a soft collision with the DEV-2904 Path A ClickHouse twin.
precedents.applicable: Do not open, edit, or reconfigure that twin from this branch.

precedents.relevance: Jira describes CH159 rows in db_error-2026-10-02.log, about 30s, for org 469. This prep did not read production logs or Cloud ClickHouse.
precedents.applicable: Out of scope to fix or re-identify that query. The before/after sample in Implement uses the new formatter against a forced local timeout, not a production chase.
